text.p: Headlines from major national newspapers. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
EL PAIS

- Government drafts new State Secrets law after Supreme Court asks state to declassify secret service documents; new law foresees creation of State Secrets commission that would oversee such decisions in future.
- KAS and youth group Jarrai form core of new shadow leadership of ETA's political wing Herri Batasuna.
EL MUNDO
- Basque separatist group ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom) asks for total of two billion pesetas to free one of its hostages, Cosme Delclaux.
- Some 10,000 demonstrate in northern city of San Sebastian for freedom of two hostages held by ETA.
- Opposition Socialists say Supreme Court should not be ruling on national security after it demands declassification of secret service documents; they say it is up to the government.
DIARIO 16
- Six year sentence of disgraced former Banesto bank chairman Mario Conde proves daily el Mundo guilty of slander.
ABC
- Squandering of regional public companies creates hole of some 476 billion pesetas.
CINCO DIAS
- Savings growth loses steam and entry of money into funds drops by third.
- Unions and employers agree to severance pay costs of 33 days per year worked.
- Madrid hospital encourages doctors to abandon advantages that come with being civil servant.
EXPANSION
- Health costs and aid to public companies will suffer most from budgetary constraint in coming years.
- Banco Santander starts year by raising dividend 15.7 percent.
- GACETA DE LOS NEGOCIOS
- Banco Santander chairman Emilio Botin reaffirms international banking model without industrial links.
- Banking institutions spent around 465 billion pesetas in buying company and industry shares in 1996.
- Industry director general Pau Guardans says government does not favour creation of hard nucleus in electricity firm Endesa before privatisation. mad mcm
